conventions.convention: The parameters p,q are coprime nonzero signed integers; the curve has angular winding (p,q) and is oriented by increasing parameter. Noncoprime parameters describe a union of parallel primitive curves.
The fixed mirror reflection conjugates the second complex coordinate, sending T(p,q) to image-oriented T(p,-q); reversing the knot orientation gives T(-p,-q).

The exterior uses a sufficiently small invariant round-metric tube. The positive meridian bounds an oriented normal disk; the preferred longitude has degree one around the knot and zero exterior homology. With pα+qβ=1, μ=y^αx^β and λ=hμ^(-pq).

The Alexander module uses positive-meridian deck action. The polynomial is determined by E0 of the absolute Alexander module, up to units ±t^k; it is distinct from the knot-normalized fraction Δ/(1-t).
The geometric definition, unit-slope, sign-change and Hopf-plumbing items assume countable choice; the group, Alexander, genus-formula and worked-example items assume full AC.

load_bearing.statement: For coprime nonzero integers p,q, T(p,q) is the oriented parameterized primitive slope pα+qβ on the standard unknotted Heegaard torus; the fixed mirror conjugates the second complex coordinate.

Assume full AC and coprime nonzero integers p,q. The specified torus-knot exterior has group ⟨x,y | x^p=y^q⟩, central regular fiber h=x^p=y^q, and a Seifert fibration over a disk with core multiplicities |p|,|q|. For pα+qβ=1, compatible based paths give μ=y^αx^β and λ=hμ^(-pq).

Assume full AC and coprime nonzero integers p,q. The quotient δ=(t^(pq)-1)(t-1)/((t^p-1)(t^q-1)) is Laurent polynomial, the positive-meridian Alexander module of T(p,q) is Λ/(δ), and Δ is associated to δ.

Assume countable choice and coprime integers p,q≥2. There is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary T(p,q), genus (p-1)(q-1)/2, constructed from a disk by plumbing (p-1)(q-1) positive Hopf bands.
Assume full AC and coprime nonzero integers p,q; put a=|p|, b=|q|. Then δ_(a,b)=(t^(ab)-1)(t-1)/((t^a-1)(t^b-1)) belongs to Z[t], Δ_T(p,q) is associated to δ_(a,b), and g(T(p,q))=(a-1)(b-1)/2.

concerns.concern: Proof 4.2 says that m has abelianization -1 under x↦q,y↦p, 'so it is opposite the positive normal-disk meridian, whose class is the positive generator by [F3].' F3 establishes generation by the geometric positive meridian, but does not calibrate its sign against this newly chosen algebraic isomorphism to Z. The proof needs the short geometric orientation/linking check that the positively oriented coordinate cores x,y have linking q,p with the explicitly oriented K. Proof 5.1 currently refers back to 4.2 for that calibration.

seams_checked.note: The chosen tube, normal-disk meridian, degree-one null-homologous longitude, boundary basis and exterior retraction match the opened suppliers. The local algebraic sign-calibration gap is recorded separately.

The unit-slope lemma uses the supplied standard oriented unknot convention. The genus proof uses exactly the mirror/reversal genus-invariance statement, with its countable-choice hypothesis discharged.
The determinant and genus-bound suppliers use E0 of the positive-meridian Alexander module, Laurent-unit equivalence and exponent width. The torus-knot proof preserves these conventions and full AC.

The A-page inventory has no direct citation to the assigned torus-knot items. Its worked companion example ex-knot-kt-17-worked-cases faithfully uses the trefoil presentation and λ=hμ^(-6), obtaining fiber slope λ+6μ; its diagram carries that same slope.

The actual edge is through def-coprime-torus-knot in lem-epsilon-stable-equivalence-and-not-a-homomorphism. Its geometric admissions use the positive complex-coordinate torus curves and the positive trefoil convention; they do not attribute Floer computations or cabling results to the torus-knot supplier.
